title: Digital sovereignty in professional translation workflows: a case study of migrating from Windows to Linux
abstract: arXiv:2610.41561v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study examines digital sovereignty in professional translation through a screening of computer-assisted translation tools and translation management systems, and a case study of migrating a translator's workstation from Windows to Linux. The framework combines three principles - Control, Continuity and Exit - with three practical requirements: native Linux operation, independence from mandatory external services, and independent access to essential data and resources. Drawing on documentary evidence and the limited number of responses received from providers, the ecosystem screening distinguishes Linux accessibility from operational independence: browser-based platforms may remain dependent on provider-controlled infrastructure. translated_title: 专业翻译工作流中的数字主权：从Windows迁移到Linux的案例研究
translated_abstract: 本研究通过筛选计算机辅助翻译工具和翻译管理系统，并以一个将译者工作站从Windows迁移到Linux的案例研究，考察了专业翻译中的数字主权问题。该框架结合三项原则——控制、连续性与退出——以及三项实践要求：Linux本地原生运行、独立于强制性外部服务，以及对关键数据和资源的独立访问。基于文献证据和从服务商处获得的有限回应，生态系统筛选区分了“Linux可访问性”与“运营独立性”：基于浏览器的平台可能仍然依赖于服务商控制的基础设施。迁移案例展示了围绕可本地运行的Linux核心重构专业翻译工作流的可行性，使用了LoopCAT、LibreOffice和本地运行的TranslateGemma，以及其他工具……
tldr: 本研究提出以“控制、连续性、退出”三原则结合三项实践要求的数字主权评估框架，并通过将译者工作站从Windows迁移至Linux（采用LoopCAT、LibreOffice和本地运行的TranslateGemma）的案例研究，证明了专业翻译工作流可在可本地运行的Linux核心上实现重构。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a digital sovereignty framework combining the principles of Control, Continuity, and Exit with three practical requirements, and demonstrates through a Windows-to-Linux workstation migration case study that professional translation workflows can be feasibly reconstructed around a locally operable Linux core.
